The successful candidate will be a collaborative and entrepreneurial leader who can lead through influence, navigate complex stakeholder environments, and build alignment around shared priorities. As a champion for Central Alberta’s skilled trades ecosystem, the Director will be responsible for maintaining momentum across the Coalition, securing resources, advancing strategic initiatives, and demonstrating measurable progress toward the Strategy’s objectives.

**Strategic Leadership & Implementation**

* Lead the implementation and ongoing advancement of the Central Alberta Trades Strategy, translating strategic priorities into annual objectives, implementation plans, measurable outcomes, and deliverables.
* Oversee multiple concurrent initiatives, including priorities, resources, timelines, budgets, performance, and outcomes, while proactively identifying and mitigating risks.
* Monitor emerging trends, opportunities, and challenges affecting the skilled trades ecosystem and provide recommendations to the Governance Committee.

**Coalition Leadership & Partnership Development**

* Serve as the primary coordinator and relationship-builder for the CATS Coalition, fostering strong, trusted relationships with industry, employers, educational institutions, governments, municipalities, Indigenous communities, workforce development organizations, and community partners.
* Facilitate cross-sector collaboration to align priorities, reduce duplication, leverage resources, and advance collective action.
* Serve as an ambassador and spokesperson for CATS and its working groups.

**Funding Development & Sustainability**

* Lead the identification, development, and pursuit of funding and investment opportunities from government, industry, philanthropic, and other external sources.
* Develop grant applications, business cases, sponsorship proposals, partnership agreements, and sustainable funding approaches that support long-term Strategy implementation.
* Build relationships with current and prospective funders and ensure funding commitments, reporting, and accountability requirements are effectively managed.

**Performance Measurement, Reporting & Continuous Improvement**

* Establish and monitor measures of progress and performance aligned with the Strategy’s priorities and expected outcomes.
* Coordinate data collection, analysis, and reporting across participating organizations, using evidence to support decision-making and continuous improvement.
* Provide regular reporting on progress, performance, risks, funding, and outcomes to the Governance Committee, funders, and other stakeholders.

**Advocacy & Regional Leadership**

* Champion the skilled trades as a critical contributor to the **economic and social prosperity and long-term sustainability of Central Alberta**.
* Maintain awareness of developments across industry, education, workforce development, government policy, and the broader skilled trades environment to identify opportunities for regional collaboration and advocacy.

**People Leadership**

* Provide leadership within CATS for continuous improvement, innovation, industry relevance in services and strong student pathways.
* Ensure effective workforce planning, role clarity, and distribution of work

pour bâtir et diriger la fonction TI, identité et sécurité de Manmade.
  
  
Vous serez responsable de la façon dont nos employés, nos appareils et nos systèmes restent connectés, productifs et protégés : au bureau, dans notre entrepôt et dans nos magasins. Nous nous développons rapidement, les choses changent vite et une présence en interne est nécessaire.

**About the role**

[Confidential] is building a new team to deliver complete IT fit-outs of data halls, from an empty room to live, tested and documented computing capacity. Once the building shell, power and cooling are in place, our crews take the white space from A to Z: receiving and staging, rack and cabinet placement, overhead pathways, bonding and grounding, copper and high-density fibre, network and server hardware, testing, power-up and handover to the client.

As a Senior Technician, you are the go-to technical lead on site. You turn drawings and cable schedules into the day's work, run a crew of Level 2 technicians, do the hard technical work yourself, solve the problems others can't, and sign off on quality before anything is handed over. This is a working lead role: you'll spend most of your day hands-on alongside your crew.

**The scope: a full data hall fit-out, A to Z**

Every project follows the same lifecycle, and you'll lead your crew through all of it:

1. Pre-construction: Review drawings, rack elevations, cable schedules, port maps and fibre plans; confirm site readiness; flag design conflicts before work starts

2. Receiving and staging: Receive, inspect, inventory and stage racks, cabinets, cable, optics and hardware; report damaged or missing items

3. Racks and cabinets: Lay out, place, level, bolt together and anchor racks and cabinets to the floor plan; install containment, doors, side panels, blanking panels and cable managers

4. Bonding and grounding: Install and verify rack and pathway bonding to the site grounding system per drawings and standards

5. Overhead pathways: Install ladder rack, basket tray, fibre guide/runway and supports (threaded rod, Unistrut), keeping clearances and segregation to plan

6. Structured cabling: Pull, route, dress and terminate copper (Cat6/6A) and fibre, including pre-terminated MPO/MTP trunks, LC, patch panels and cassettes; maintain bend radius and fill ratios

7. Rack-and-stack: Install servers, switches, storage, GPU/AI systems, optics and rack PDUs to rack elevations; patch to port maps and cut sheets

8. Labelling and records: Label every cable, port, panel and rack to the client's scheme (TIA-606 practice); barcode-scan and record assets

9. Testing and certification: Fibre inspection and cleaning, OLTS (Tier 1) and OTDR (Tier 2) testing, copper certification, continuity and polarity checks; fix and retest any failures

10. Power-up and validation: Support power-on and green-light checks, out-of-band management connectivity, link and loopback testing, and burn-in with the client's engineers

11. Quality and handover: Run QA/QC inspections and punch lists, complete as-built drawings, test reports and asset records, and walk the client through handover

12. Ongoing work: Moves, adds and changes, migrations, decommissioning and remediation in live environments

**What you'll do**

**Lead the crew**

* Turn project plans and drawings into a clear, ordered task list and assign work to match each technician's skill level

* Run pre-task briefings and job hazard assessments before work starts each day

* Manage handoffs between crews, shifts and other trades, and keep materials and dependencies lined up so nobody is waiting

* Coach and develop Level 2 technicians on the job, check their work, and help them grow toward Level 3

* Hold the team to safety and workmanship standards, and use stop-work authority when something isn't right

* Report daily progress, blockers and material needs to the Fit-Out Manager

**Own the technical work**

* Lead installs, power-up, migrations and project closeout from start to finish

Compensation: CAD $72,000–$87,000 annual base salary, commensurate with experience, plus performance-based incentives.

**Our Purpose**

Spur Line Crop Solutions is a farmer-owned, independent agricultural business rooted in Saskatchewan, with a Western Canadian outlook. Our vision is “Helping farmers adapt to a changing agroecosystem.” Our baseline is “Farmers helping farmers.”

We work with open-minded farmers and ranchers who want to move from high-input conventional systems reliant on synthetic inputs toward farming systems that more closely emulate natural ecosystem services. We help them implement the six soil-health principles in a practical, profitable, and purposeful manner—through plant diversity, soil-health support, education, agricultural programs, and relevant products.

Our credibility comes from practice. Through research and trials at Soli Vivi Farms, the founder’s farm and ranch, we pressure-test what we recommend and share honest learning in the context of real farming conditions.

**The Opportunity: Help Build the Next Stage**

Spur Line is an early-stage business with an existing farmer network, a clear vision, and significant ambition for its next stage of growth. We are looking for an experienced professional who is energized by building—not simply maintaining—an established system.

You will not inherit a finished machine. Some processes, customer systems, and ways of working are still taking shape. The opportunity is to work from the vision set by the founder and executive team, bring your own judgment and ideas, and turn that foundation into a dependable, well-organized business that serves farmers consistently.

This means taking initiative, improving how work gets done, and owning follow-through. It also means collaborating with a small team and being willing to contribute practically as the business develops.

**A Relationship and Farmer-Extension Role**

At its core, this is a relationship-management and farmer-extension role with commercial accountability. Most of your time will be spent developing and maintaining relationships with our farmer following and with suppliers, collaborators, and industry partners.

Farmer extension means connecting useful knowledge and field experience with decisions producers can make on their own operations. You will help farmers understand options, learn from trials and demonstrations, and find the right next step or source of expertise. The relationship should offer value between purchases—not only when there is something to sell.

Plant diversity and seed are the first commercial priority, including cover crops, intercrops, annual blends, perennial forages, and our own farm-grown seed offerings. You will also connect farmers with Spur Line’s wider consulting, program, and educational resources.

Sales are a meaningful part of the job. We expect you to develop opportunities, follow up, ask for the business, and build profitable repeat relationships. Growth should come from client success and trust—not pressure to sell something that does not fit.

**What You Will Help Build**

Strong farmer relationships: proactive contact, dependable support, practical learning, and thoughtful next-season planning.

Productive industry partnerships: ongoing relationships with suppliers and collaborators that create value for farmers and Spur Line.

Profitable commercial growth: lead seed-business development and strengthen repeat business, forecasting, and gross-margin performance.

Better customer systems: help shape a CRM and relationship-management process that the team uses consistently.

Connected research and education: work with technical and marketing team members to bring trials, field learning, and farmer questions into useful conversations.

A farmer-success team: supervise summer students initially, with the intention of building and leading your own team as the business grows.

You will work with the executive team and colleagues across technical consulting, programs, marketing, administration, and operations. You are not expected to replace every specialist; you are expected to connect the right people and keep the relationship moving.

**Who We Are Looking For**

Client-success management and account-management experience are required. You should have a demonstrated ability to own ongoing relationships, understand client goals, coordinate support, and deliver on commitments.

A proven consultative-sales record is a major asset and strongly preferred, particularly where sales growth followed from customer success. Commercial confidence is essential.

We strongly value genuine passion for soil health, regenerative agriculture, plant diversity, and holistic management. The right person is personable, self-motivated, organized, open-minded, and comfortable taking responsibility before every process is perfected.

CRM experience, agricultural knowledge, partnership development, and people leadership are valuable. Above all, we need someone who combines farmer-first values with the professional discipline to turn relationships, ideas, and opportunities into consistent action.

**How and Where You Will Work**

This is a hybrid role based in south-central Saskatchewan, combining home-office work, farmer visits, and time at our farm headquarters. Some additional travel for industry events and selected opportunities will be part of the role, along with occasional practical support during busy periods.

You will have executive-team direction and collaboration, alongside room to take ownership, improve systems, and grow into broader leadership. This is an opportunity to help shape the business—not simply fill a seat in it.

****Work Location****
Hybrid, based in our Toronto or Montreal office. In-office expectations vary with business needs. If you are based in Montreal, expect to travel to Toronto a couple of times per month.

Maestro, our AI-powered underwriting platform, already runs inside nesto, with AI agents making real-time, policy-based decisions. Your mission is to run the program that puts a fleet of AI agents live in Canadian banks’ production environments. The client Sponsor makes the final call on the story.
* Chair eval review. Run the weekly review of agent performance evidence and turn it into build and tuning priorities for Engineering. Data Scientists produce the evidence. You review it and do not produce it yourself.
* Lead the model-risk relationship. Lead the relationship with the client’s model-risk team. Land validation packages for each condition family and secure the risk and governance sign-offs that authorize shadow and production.
* Run the shadow program. Adjudicate divergences, re-validate for drift, and report value foregone to client executives each month.
* Own change management and readiness. Co-own the joint readiness sign-off with the client and make sure the pilot group is trained and running the new workflow.
* Build the deployment playbook. Write the repeatable process that takes AI agents from client requirements through testing and client approval into production. Document each agent’s deployment as you go. The playbook is a core deliverable, not a retrospective.
* Protect scope. Hold client “small asks” to the config log and SOW change process. Nothing gets absorbed silently.

* You have a client-facing delivery background, as an engagement manager, Delivery Director, or Implementation Director.
* You have run senior delivery teams on client sites and led working sessions with EVP-level executives.
* You have led client AI implementations hands-on, from requirements through production.
* You know ML/AI delivery well enough to chair an eval review, question precision and recall trade-offs, and translate model evidence into language a risk committee can act on.
* You define written exit criteria, produce the artifacts that back them, and document decisions.

****Nice-to-Have****

* Experience implementing AI for banks or other regulated organizations, including model-risk validation.
* Experience implementing your own company’s product at the client.
* Mortgage or retail-credit domain knowledge, or experience with staged production rollouts of decisioning systems.
* Comfort building the playbook while running it in a scale-up.

* You have delivered AI solutions for enterprise clients on high-visibility projects and know how to earn their stakeholders’ trust.
* You get energized when there is no playbook to follow and can turn uncertainty into a clear, structured approach.
* You do well under high expectations on a project that matters deeply to the client.

* Orchestrer l’exécution interfonctionnelle entre les équipes de construction, d’ingénierie, de mise en service, d’approvisionnement et de contrôle de programme afin d’assurer l’alignement sur les objectifs du programme.

**Ce que vous ferez**

* Soutenir la direction de l’architecture technologique dans la mise en œuvre des stratégies, des priorités et des feuilles de route établies en les traduisant en activités et jalons, et en définissant clairement les dépendances et les responsabilités à l’échelle de la fonction
* Maintenir une vue d’ensemble des priorités et des activités de l’architecture technologique pour soutenir la planification et la prise de décisions de la direction
* Appuyer l’analyse, la planification et la coordination des priorités émergentes et des initiatives spéciales en reliant les plans d’architecture technologique aux priorités globales du STI et du cabinet
* Servir de point de coordination central entre les activités liées à l’architecture, au développement, à la mise en œuvre et aux opérations, y compris pour ce qui touche les dépendances, le séquencement des tâches, les décisions et les transferts entre les architectes, les responsables techniques et les équipes de mise en œuvre
* Veiller à ce que les décisions et les priorités en matière d’architecture soient prises en compte dans la planification et l’exécution de la mise en œuvre
* Participer à la coordination des activités d’architecture technologique entre les différentes fonctions, ainsi qu’à l’échelle du cabinet canadien et de l’organisation mondiale
* Établir des modes de fonctionnement efficaces qui aident l’équipe à gérer les priorités, les décisions, les risques, les mesures à prendre et les dépendances, et à assurer le suivi des mesures et des engagements convenus
* Repérer les occasions de simplifier les processus, d’améliorer les méthodes de travail et de renforcer la coordination au sein de l’équipe
* Fournir à la direction une vision intégrée des besoins, des activités et des dépendances pour appuyer une planification efficace des ressources et des priorités
* Appuyer la coordination et la réalisation des initiatives d’architecture technologique en établissant clairement les résultats, les jalons, les responsables, les dépendances et les risques, en particulier lorsque le travail nécessite la collaboration des équipes d’architecture et de mise en œuvre
* Travailler de concert avec le bureau de gestion de projets et les gestionnaires de projet désignés pour les initiatives nécessitant une gouvernance officielle, et porter à l’attention de la direction les risques, les contraintes et les décisions exigeant son intervention
* Fournir à la direction de l’architecture technologique des mises à jour concises axées sur la prise de décisions concernant les priorités, les progrès, les risques et les enjeux
* Assurer la coordination avec les autres équipes du STI au pays et ailleurs dans le monde, les directeurs de la Technologie des différentes fonctions et les parties prenantes concernées pour atteindre les objectifs en matière d’architecture technologique
* Préparer et animer des séances de planification d’équipe, des revues de direction, des séances de travail et d’autres rencontres de coordination; communiquer clairement les questions techniques et les enjeux liés à la réalisation des initiatives aux parties prenantes techniques et non techniques

* Baccalauréat en informatique, en génie, en systèmes d’information, en gestion des technologies, en affaires ou dans un domaine connexe (ou expérience pratique équivalente)
* Expérience considérable dans des environnements technologiques, idéalement dans les domaines de la prestation de services technologiques, de l’optimisation de l’architecture, des opérations technologiques ou des domaines connexes

* Expérience de la coordination d’initiatives technologiques complexes faisant intervenir plusieurs équipes, parties prenantes et dépendances
* Grand sens de l’organisation, excellent jugement et fortes aptitudes en communication; capacité à structurer, à clarifier et à faire progresser des travaux complexes ou ambigus, et à travailler efficacement avec des leaders en technologie, des architectes, des spécialistes techniques et des professionnels de la gestion de projet

Contact prospective clients, assess fit and explain the value of Swift's services.

**15% Inbound Client Support**

Respond to client questions and provide timely support by phone, email and text.

Move onboarded clients through the approximately 120-day application process.

* Quality monitoring: Spot-check Arabic items, identify quality issues, provide ongoing feedback through DMs, and escalate recurring or critical issues.

* Strong grasp of the English language to follow project guidelines, communicate with teams, and provide clear feedback in English.
* 3+ years of professional experience in Arabic writing, editing, translation, localization, content QA, AI training, education, annotation, or related language-review workflows.
* Strong understanding of Arabic grammar, spelling conventions, punctuation, diacritics, RTL formatting, tone, register, Modern Standard Arabic, and regional Arabic variation.

**Head of Engineering Job Description:** Scope, Impact & Qualifications Reports to: CEO Level: Executive (CTO-equivalent scope) Org size: ~25 engineers Time split: 70% Product / 30% Discipline ROLE SUMMARY The Head of Engineering owns the technical outcomes of Maestro's entire product suite while also serving as the top of the engineering discipline ladder: every engineering manager and individual contributor ultimately ladders up to this role. The position deliberately splits attention: 70% product execution, 30% discipline accountability. Product delivery is the immediate, ongoing accountability; discipline work compounds over time and requires protected but smaller blocks of focus so it doesn't get crowded out by delivery pressure. This role sits at the center of Maestro's matrix structure, accountable for craft quality and standards company-wide, while ensuring embedded engineering talent on each product team is pointed at the right priorities.
  
  
**SCOPE • Org reach:** all engineering leads across all product lines report into this role (directly or via a lead layer), the senior-most engineering accountability in the company. • Product surface: full product suite, every active product line's engineering output. • Discipline surface: engineering-wide standards, tooling, and process, independent of which product team an engineer sits on. THE 70%: PRODUCT ACCOUNTABILITY The Head of Engineering is the single accountable owner for engineering execution across Maestro's product portfolio.
  
  
**What this looks like day to day:** • Partners with the engineering leads of every product line to ensure their teams are resourced against the right priorities: not just busy, but correctly sequenced. • Accountable for ensuring product strategy and roadmap direction are translated into clear, actionable engineering plans, serving as the connective layer between Product and Delivery leadership and the engineering organization, primarily through engineering leads embedded within product teams. • Accountable for applying technical judgment to turn high-level strategic priorities into concrete technical execution plans, enabling and guiding engineering leads to scope, sequence, and de-risk delivery across their product areas. • Identifies where product priorities and engineering capacity are misaligned across teams and resolves the tradeoff, including cross-team resourcing calls.
  
  

* Is the escalation point when a product line's engineering execution is off track, and is accountable for getting it back on track. Impact: Every product line ships against strategy, not just against what's easiest to build. Product and Delivery leaders have one accountable engineering partner instead of negotiating separately with each product line's lead. THE 30%: DISCIPLINE ACCOUNTABILITY The Head of Engineering owns what "good engineering" means at Maestro, independent of the product line.

**What this looks like day to day:** • Sets and maintains company-wide engineering standards (code quality, architecture principles, technical debt posture). • Owns cross-cutting technical initiatives that no single product team should solve independently, e.g. product suite services and universal QA automation. • Defines how AI tooling is used across engineering, including guardrails to ensure AI usage improves output quality and velocity rather than introducing risk or degrading craft.
  
  

* Identifies and removes friction in how engineering work gets done company-wide, streamlining processes that slow every team down in the same way. • Is the ultimate accountable owner for engineering management practice (how EMs lead, how performance is evaluated, how the craft is grown) even where day-to-day people management is embedded in product teams. Impact: Engineering quality, velocity, and management practice don't fragment by product line. An engineer's experience of "how we build software here" is consistent no matter which team they're on, and the org gets the benefits of scale (shared tooling, shared standards) instead of each team reinventing its own.

SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE • Engineers across the organization deliver flawless technical execution that earns long-term client retention and supports growth. • Product lines are resourced against strategic priority, with tradeoffs made explicitly rather than by default. • Engineering leads across product lines operate with a shared technical bar and shared tooling. • Company-wide initiatives (QA automation, AI usage standards) ship and get adopted, not just get designed.
  
  

* Engineering management practice is consistent and healthy across the org, even though EMs are embedded in product teams day to day. QUALIFICATIONS Maestro hires for demonstrated capability, not years-of-service checkboxes. The bar below is competency-based: what someone needs to be able to do, not how long they've been doing it. Required competencies: • Has personally carried end-to-end accountability for engineering delivery across more than one product or team simultaneously: not just led a single team, but balanced competing priorities across several.
* Can translate ambiguous, high-level strategy (from product, business, or leadership) into a technical execution plan that engineers can actually build against, without needing someone else to do that translation. • Has designed or materially improved an engineering standard, process, or tooling investment that worked across teams (not a single-team fix) and can point to the before/after. • Comfortably operates in a matrixed environment, influencing and aligning engineering leads, their teams, and cross-functional stakeholders without relying on formal authority. • Has hands-on technical depth sufficient to earn credibility with senior engineers and to personally evaluate technical tradeoffs.

This is not a purely managerial role. • Has direct experience managing or mentoring engineering managers, not only individual contributors. • Demonstrates sound judgment on when to standardize company-wide versus when to let product teams operate with autonomy. Strongly preferred: • Experience operating at this scope inside a company of comparable size (roughly 15 to 50 engineers), where formal process is lighter and judgment calls happen more often than policy lookups.
  
  

* Direct experience setting a company's approach to AI-assisted engineering (tooling choices, guardrails, or usage standards) rather than just using AI tools personally. • A track record of building or scaling QA automation, testing strategy, or release process across multiple teams. • Experience partnering directly with Product and Delivery leadership as a peer, not just receiving requirements from them. • Experience leading engineering for always-on, customer-facing digital products or live-service platforms, where availability, release discipline, observability, incident response, and rapid cross-functional coordination directly affect the end-user experience and client retention.

**What we're explicitly not requiring:** • A specific prior title (VP Engineering, CTO, etc.). We care about scope actually carried, not the title it came with. • A minimum years-of-experience threshold. Competency and evidence of impact matter more than tenure.
  
  

* Deep expertise in every technology in Maestro's stack. Technical judgment and the ability to evaluate tradeoffs matter more than hands-on fluency in any one language or framework.

The Director of IT Service Management leads the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of Hertz’s global IT service management practices. This role turns technology and business priorities into reliable, measurable service operations, supporting a consistent experience for employees and business partners across the company.
  
  
Working with Technology and business leaders, the Director oversees key service management processes and the systems that support them, including ServiceNow. The role partners closely with infrastructure, end-user services, application, cybersecurity, and operations teams to improve service quality, system stability, resiliency, and compliance. It also manages team performance, budgets, and vendor relationships within the scope of responsibility, using operational data and service metrics to guide decisions and improvements.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Lead, develop, and motivate the IT Service Management team, setting clear goals and supporting employee growth and technical capability.
* Translate business and Technology priorities into service management plans, operational goals, and measurable outcomes .
* Develop and maintain an innovative IT Service Management roadmap that prioritizes automation and modernizes processes, tools, and service delivery in support of Hertz’s business and Technology goals.
* Lead and continuously improve service management processes, including Incident, Request, Problem, Change, Service Level, Event, Service Catalog, and Configuration Management (CMDB).
* Use KPIs, service data, and customer feedback to identify performance gaps, manage backlogs, and prioritize process and system improvements.
* Oversee the ServiceNow platform roadmap and backlog, partnering with stakeholders on enhancements, automation, integrations, and adoption.
* Work with Technology and business leaders to improve service quality, operational readiness, system stability, and resiliency.
* Manage the service management budget and assigned resources, balancing service needs, risk, and cost.
* Set expectations for vendors and service providers supporting ITSM processes; monitor service levels, delivery, governance, and cost-effectiveness.
* Ensure service management policies and procedures reflect current practices and support compliance with applicable requirements, including SOX, PCI, IT audit, GDPR, and CCPA.
* Identify relevant technology and industry developments, including ITIL 4, ServiceNow, and DevOps practices, and assess their value to Hertz.
* Communicate service performance, risks, priorities, and improvement plans clearly to executives, business partners, employees, and vendors.
* Build effective working relationships across Technology and the business to coordinate service ownership and resolve operational issues.

**What We’re Looking For**

**About Neurophos**
===================

The demand for new data centers and AI compute is rapidly outpacing the planet's energy capacity. Digital solutions are hitting a power wall as we approach the physical limits of traditional silicon. Conquering this bottleneck means rethinking the fundamental architecture of inference compute. The industry's current path can't meet the need, so we're taking a different approach.

Instead of traditional electronic circuits, we use silicon photonics and an active, programmable metasurface to perform matrix multiplications at the speed of light. Our optical cells are 10,000x smaller than traditional photonic components, enabling unprecedented density. By using photonics instead of electricity, our chips become more efficient as they scale. This architecture will deliver up to 100 times the energy efficiency of existing solutions while significantly improving performance for large-scale AI inference.

We’ve assembled a world-class team of industry veterans and recently raised a $110M Series A led by Gates Frontier. Participants include M12 (Microsoft’s Venture Fund), Carbon Direct Capital, Aramco Ventures, Bosch Ventures, Tectonic Ventures, Space Capital, and others.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**
  
The Orange County Information Technology (OCIT)- Strategy, Innovation, & Architecture division is seeking an experienced and strategic individual who will oversee and assist a team of Network and Voice Services Delivery Managers in the development of network and system designs, adopting network requirements, coordinating network planning, and maintaining a stable networking environment. Responsibilities and duties for this position include, but are not limited to, the following:  
  
  

* Providing technical oversight to contracted vendors on network operations and implementations

* Designing reliable and cost-effective network services including email transport, domain name services, directory services, and digital certificate services
* Managing financial, vendor, and organizational resources including budgets, expenditures, and contracts to achieve County business objectives
* Planning the connection of new sites to the County's data network
* Specifying required equipment for installation activities
* Utilizing project organization management including scheduling, milestones, deliverables to achieve successful outcomes
* Traveling throughout Orange County and attending staff meetings as needed, along with performing related duties as assigned

**Technical Knowledge****| Technical Expertise**
  

* Understanding of Cisco SD-WAN, Meraki, and ACI solutions
* Proficiency with Cisco ASR/ISR/Catalyst routers and Cisco Catalyst/Nexus switches
* Applying advanced networking and VolP/WebEx expertise, including SIP (Session Initiation Protocol), RTP/RTCP, H.323, TCP/IP, VLANs, QoS prioritization, and routing protocols (OSPF, BGP) to ensure call signaling, media transport, and overall service quality
* Leading IT projects and operational initiatives, including prioritizing competing demands, resource planning, forecasting fiscal expenditures, and ongoing vendor and contract management

POSITION SUMMARY

DEPLOY has been retained to find an Information Security Manager to lead the information security program and report to the Director of Information Technology. The Information Security Manager owns security governance and risk management, third-party risk, incident response, and the day-to-day operation of the enterprise security technology stack.

This is a hands-on leadership role. This position is expected to operate comfortably at a technical level while working with IT leadership and business management across a decentralized family of companies to align security priorities with business objectives. Success depends as much on influence, relationship-building, and the clear communication of risk as it does on technical depth.

This position supervises internal security staff and manages outsourced security service providers and is accountable for leading security projects from definition through delivery.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

Security Governance, Risk and Compliance

Operate and mature the enterprise security program in partnership with the Director of IT, aligning security investments and projects to identified risks and business requirements.

Direct recurring risk assessments and control audits across all operations and its affiliate companies; maintain the enterprise risk register and drive remediation items to closure.

Develop, maintain, and socialize security policies, standards, and procedures, mapping controls to a recognized framework (NIST 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, and or CMMC) and keeping documentation audit- ready.

Own responses to customer security questionnaires, cyber insurance applications and attestations, and contractual or regulatory security obligations (e.g., CMMC, customer-specific requirements).

Assist resource owners and IT staff at affiliate companies in understanding and remediating security audit findings reported by internal and external auditors.

**Threat Detection, Incident Response and Security Operations**

Manage high-severity incident response end to end, including triage, containment, forensic analysis, executive communication, and post-incident review.

Maintain and regularly test the incident response plan and supporting playbooks; coordinate tabletop exercises with IT and business leadership.

Direct the operational management of vulnerability management, SIEM and managed detection and response services, threat intelligence platforms, and dark web monitoring.

Manage MSSP and security vendor performance against service levels, escalating and remediating gaps in coverage or responsiveness.

**Security Architecture and Technology**

Ensure consistent application of security standards and provide configuration guidance and change control for firewall, asset management, endpoint, and backup and recovery systems.

Strengthen identity and cloud security across the Microsoft estate, including Active Directory and Entra ID, Conditional Access, privileged access management, Microsoft Defender, Intune, and overall Microsoft 365 and SaaS security posture.

Partner with plant and operations leadership to extend asset visibility, network segmentation, and monitoring into OT/ICS and manufacturing environments, accounting for the availability and safety constraints unique to plant-floor systems.

Evaluate, pilot, and recommend new security technologies, and lead their implementation across ONI and affiliate environments.

Data Protection and Emerging Technology Governance

Lead data classification, data loss prevention, and insider risk initiatives, prioritizing protection of the company's most sensitive business and customer information.

Establish and maintain governance for artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies, including acceptable use standards, data handling requirements, vendor and model review, and monitoring for unsanctioned tool usage.

**Third-Party and Vendor Risk**

Oversee third-party risk assessments, including vendor due diligence, security and privacy terms in contracts, and ongoing monitoring of critical suppliers and service providers.

Maintain an inventory of third parties with access to ONI systems or data, along with the assessed risk associated with each.

**Leadership, Awareness and Reporting**

Supervise the Cybersecurity Engineer and other assigned security staff — setting objectives, guiding performance, and supporting professional development.

Manage the delivery and measure the effectiveness of security awareness and training programs, including phishing simulation and role-based training.

Lead the reporting and analysis of cybersecurity metrics and KPIs for both operational and executive audiences, including periodic updates to senior leadership.

Lead cross-functional project teams, defining scope, schedule, and resource requirements, and delivering security projects on time and on budget.

**REQUIRED SKILLS, ABILITIES AND EDUCATION**

A minimum of five years of IT experience, including at least three years in a dedicated information security role and at least two years in a supervisory or team-lead capacity.

Bachelor's degree or higher in Cybersecurity, Information Security, Information Systems, Engineering,

Computer Science, or a related field of study. Equivalent experience combined with relevant certification will be considered.

Demonstrated experience in risk assessment, incident management, and project management.

Working knowledge of a recognized security framework (NIST 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, CMMC, CIS Controls, or ISO 27001) and experience mapping controls and evidence to it.

Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical risk into business terms for non-technical audiences.

Hands-on familiarity with core security technologies, including SIEM, endpoint detection and response, vulnerability management, firewalls, email security, identity and access management, and backup and recovery.

Experience securing a Microsoft enterprise environment, including Active Directory and Entra ID, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Defender, and Intune.

Strong leadership skills and the ability to work effectively with business managers, IT engineering, and IT operations staff.

Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.

The ability to interact with ONI and affiliate company personnel, build strong relationships at all levels and across all business units, and understand business imperatives.

A desire to explore and learn new things.

**About the Role:**

The Technical Program Manager administers the qualification and validation of new products, and of retrofits and engineering changes to existing parts, for use in large-scale data center environments. The program spans inside plant (ISP) and outside plant (OSP) optical fiber cable, connectivity, and pathway products from candidate identification through validated, released configuration. The position owns the technical content of the program: product selection and evaluation criteria, test methodology, acceptance limits, measurement integrity, and the qualification record that supports product approval and release. The Technical Program Manager serves as the technical interface between design engineering, construction and installation crews, component manufacturers, and test equipment suppliers, and is accountable for validated, documented, and field-reproducible connectivity products on schedule.

**What You’ll Do:**

* **Validation Program Planning and Execution:** Develop and own integrated validation program plans covering both new product introduction and retrofits or engineering changes to existing parts — qualification sequence, entry and exit criteria, material and laboratory dependencies, and decision gates — holding the critical path and driving programs to documented closure.
* **Inside Plant and Outside Plant Infrastructure:** Manage ISP structured cabling across backbone and horizontal distribution, riser and plenum pathways, main and intermediate distribution frames (MDF/IDF), cabinet and rack-mounted patch fields, fiber distribution frames, splice and termination enclosures, cassette-based modular patching, cable tray, basket and innerduct pathway, and firestopping and pathway segregation; and OSP placement across duct bank and conduit, microduct and air-blown fiber, maintenance holes and handholes, aerial and direct-buried routes, building entrance facilities and points of entry (MPOE), transition splice points, armored and dielectric constructions, and environmental and ingress protection at the ISP/OSP demarcation.
* **Fiber Cable, Connectivity, and Termination Scope:** Qualify single-mode (OS2, 9/125 µm) and multimode cable across the full range of standard counts in general industry use, from 24-fiber distribution cable through 3456-fiber high-count backbone, in loose tube, central core, ribbon, rollable ribbon, and 200/250 µm coating designs, evaluating diameter, bend radius, pulling tension, duct fill, and mid-span access against pathway and installation constraints. Own connectivity across LC and LC duplex, MTP/MPO single-row and dual-row arrays (8, 12, 16, and 24 fiber), and very-high-density MMC arrays (16 and 24 fiber), including pinned (male) and unpinned (female) configurations, UPC and APC endface geometries, gender and key orientation, and polarity schemes spanning TIA-568 Method A, B, and C and the conventions applicable to multi-row arrays. Define and validate patch panel, cassette, adapter plate, and shelf configurations for port density, fiber management, bend radius protection, slack storage, labeling access, and serviceability, and evaluate breakout, fanout, harness, trunk, and pigtail assemblies against port mapping and channel performance requirements.
* **Test, Measurement, and Acceptance:** Establish and govern optical test programs — Tier 1 optical loss test set (OLTS) insertion loss and return loss certification, Tier 2 OTDR characterization, bidirectional testing, length and continuity verification, polarity and fitment verification, and endface inspection and cleaning to recognized criteria such as IEC 61300-3-35 — controlling test reference cord (TRC) grade, referencing method, and calibration state so results are repeatable and defensible. Reconcile measured channel performance against design acceptance criteria and transceiver link specifications, and drive corrective action where acceptance limits are not met.
* **Supplier Qualification and Test Equipment Capability:** Lead technical qualification of cable, connectivity, and pathway manufacturers through sample submission, first-article inspection, mechanical and optical evaluation, failure analysis, root cause determination, and corrective action closure, maintaining a defensible qualification record and a clear statement of remaining gaps per supplier. Evaluate, select, and introduce fiber test and inspection platforms end to end, covering technical evaluation against requirements, procurement support, asset control and inventory, calibration and reference cord management, operator training, and fleet distribution to regional field crews.
* **Documentation and Standards:** Produce and sustain installation work instructions, test procedures, golden samples, first-of-kind build documentation, labeling and administration schemes, and as-built records, maintaining them so methods are applied consistently by field crews and subcontractors without procedural drift.
* **Program Governance and Risk Management:** Maintain accurate program status, ownership, target dates, and documented reasons for schedule movement, and produce recurring technical status reporting for client and internal leadership, surfacing aging, blocked, and unassigned work rather than allowing it to persist. Identify technical, schedule, supply chain, and capability risks in advance, quantify impact, drive mitigation to a named owner and committed date, and escalate with a recommendation.
* **Safety and Regulatory Compliance:** Champion a zero-injury culture in laboratory and field environments, ensuring personnel and subcontractors understand and apply laser safety, confined space, excavation, aerial work, and fiber handling requirements, and that work complies with OSHA and other applicable regulations and site access requirements.

The Technical Account Manager (TAM) serves as the Pod Leader within a matrix-organized MSP/MSSP service delivery model. The TAM owns a dedicated "pod" of technical staff and a defined book of assigned clients and is accountable for both the technical delivery quality and financial profitability of that pod.

The TAM must coordinate closely with Service Delivery Managers across all tiers to keep the pod properly staffed, trained, and aligned to each client's contracted service levels. The TAM must also work closely with Sales for client account health and profitability while also facilitating growth and retention.

**AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY**

The TAM is accountable across the following domains:

* Client Communication & Relationship Management
* Tier 1 (Service Desk), Tier 2 Support and Tier 3 Engineering Staffing & Service delivery
* Account-level performance and adherence to ManageIT and AugmentIT agreements
* Process, Documentation & Knowledgebase Maintenance (e.g. client Playbooks)
* Vendor Coordination & Escalation Support
* Agreement level profitability and service delivery KPIs
* Pod financial(P&L) and operational performance (Utilization/SLA/KPI)

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

**Client & Account Ownership**

* Own the client relationship from a technical/operational standpoint, including QBRs, escalations, and renewal risk management.
* Develop deep knowledge of each assigned client’s IT environment, business workflows, and recurring technical challenges
* Build trusted relationships with client contacts through consistent, transparent, and courteous communication.

* Drive Client-specific processes and procedures such as new hire onboarding, terminations, PC setups and security approval processes.
* Actively participate in client updates or regularly scheduled engineering reviews
* Manage the turnover to production of new services, projects or consulting engagements for assigned clients

**Pod Leadership**

* Lead 10-15 pod members consisting of Service Desk, Tier 2 Support, and Engineering staff.
* Set Pod priorities and balance workload across clients for pod to meet operational metrics
* Drive service delivery KPIs that exceeds client established SLAs such as Response time, Resolution time, CSAT and utilization.
* Manage daily support operations with client escalations across the 3-tier support pod.
* Coordinate with shared/leveraged service pods (After-Hours Desk, Tools Support, Dedicated Engineer, Depot) to ensure seamless handoffs and consistent client experience.

* Own Pod P&L performance based upon assigned client revenue against pod resource and leverage costs.
* Identify and act on Pod margin erosion, under-utilized capacity, or unbillable overage trends.
* Perform client profitability reviews and improvement recommendations with sales

* This role will be exposed to highly confidential internal and client information and will be subject to additional confidentiality requirements.

* Act as daily operational leader over a Pod of 10-15 resources, holding each team member accountable to the processes and procedures to support assigned clients.

* The TAM does not have sole hiring/firing authority but is the primary voice whose suggestions and recommendations as to the hiring, firing, advancement, promotion, or any other change of status of reporting staff carries heavy weight.

**About LawnStarter**

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, spanning three brands: LawnStarter, Lawn Love, and Home Gnome. We've cleared $750M in bookings and turned a profit three years running. Founded in Austin in 2013, we're a team of about 180 that scales past 500 employees during peak season. The marketplace itself is easy to describe and hard to run well: a customer requests a service, we price the job and match it to an eligible Pro, the Pro claims and completes the work, and we process payment and take a commission.

We're entering the most ambitious stretch in the company's history as we build new verticals, new software products, and the groundwork to become a multi-billion-dollar company.

One of our company values is AI or Extinction: every task, AI-first. No exceptions, no excuses. Top 1% or we're already a fossil. This role is hired against that bar.

**The Role**

This is a biz ops generalist role, built for someone who wants to work across many parts of the business instead of owning one narrow lane. You'll start as an individual contributor with no direct reports, in a new seat reporting directly to the COO. Your first owned area will be building Service Delivery into a working operational function. This will entail adding structure, visibility and process to the way we ensure as many customer jobs as possible are completed successfully and on time by LawnStarter Pros, in lawn care and other services we offer now and over time.

New projects will show up unscoped over time. That's by design. As LawnStarter enters new verticals and grows toward a multi-billion-dollar future, big problems will keep surfacing with no obvious owner, and you'll be one of the people the COO trusts to run them down.

**What makes this role different:**

* You work on some of the biggest company-wide projects, cutting across teams and functional areas.
* You'll be a top builder in Brain, LawnStarter's internal AI toolkit built on Claude Code that already powers everything we do across the company: metric queries, document drafting, bug triage, and more. We expect you to approach your work in an AI-first fashion, leveraging Brain to build new systems and processes that will push the limits of how fast AI can accelerate business results. Every project you run is built AI-first: the analysis, the tooling, the process automation, the monitoring. You build it yourself instead of waiting on an analyst or engineer.
* You own outcomes end to end, from recommendation through execution. Strategy without follow-through doesn't count here.

**What You'll Own**

* **Service Delivery, from the ground up.** Despite LawnStarter's considerable scale and reach, Service Delivery doesn't exist yet as a dedicated function. You'll help define the standards we should meet for job completion rates and speed, measure whether we hit them, and design processes, incentives and real-time interventions that get tested with Pros and customers in the field to lift performance. Scope covers every vertical and every delivery model, from today's 1099 Pros to potential W-2 crews under future evaluation.
* **Raising customer & Pro retention rates.** When we deliver service with excellence, Pros and customers alike stay with us longer. Working tightly with peers across Product, Data and Support, you'll identify new opportunities for us to boost retention and LTV and play a key role in driving resulting initiatives cross-functionally.
* **Whatever comes next.** New projects will land on your plate as the company grows into new verticals and builds new software products. You'll take them from "we should look into this" to building and then running systems with structure, KPIs and owners.

**Problems to Solve**

**Build a Service Delivery function that doesn't exist yet.** Right now, no one formally owns whether LawnStarter delivers the service it promises. You'll define the standard for what a Pro should deliver, then build the agents and pipelines that measure adherence to it and run the tests that change behaviors and outcomes in the field.

**Move metrics.** Leverage systems thinking and AI expertise to drive business results that sit across various functional teams. That means untangling handoffs where several teams touch a problem or goal and no one team owns the outcome.

**Take unscoped problems from ideas to fully-running and automated systems.** Some of the most important work here hasn't been named yet. At some point, someone will raise a fuzzy, unframed problem and say it needs attention. Your job is to take that starting point and build whatever tooling or process it needs, at record speed, and hand back something that runs, with a clear owner and quantitative targets attached.

**What Success Looks Like (Year 1)**

* Service Delivery is a working function with a defined (and elevated) service standard, a way to measure adherence to it, clear SOPs, and an intervention and incentive playbook that's been tested and proven to lift results.
* At least one project nobody had scoped a year earlier has gone from "we should look into this" to a heavily-automated, running system with a named owner and tracked KPIs.
* Tools you built with AI are in daily use by people other than you, and the way you work has raised the bar for how the company uses AI.
* The COO can hand you a gray-area problem with no playbook and trust that what comes back is data, a recommendation, and a plan to execute it.

**Who You Are**

**An elite AI builder.** You think in terms of agentic systems. Building agents, evals, context engineering, and thinking in guardrails are core to who you are. You keep up with the frontier and put new capabilities to work within days, not quarters. You'd be in the top few percent of AI users at any company you've worked at. **Lead the business of one of Michigan’s great four-season communities**

Lakes of the North Association is one of Michigan’s largest private residential property

owners associations: approximately 8,000 properties with over 5000 members on roughly

10,000 acres of forest, trails, and inland lakes in Antrim and Otsego Counties, southwest of

Gaylord. We operate a wide range of amenities for our members and the public, including

an 18-hole golf course with driving range and pro shop, a full-service restaurant and tavern

open the public year-round, a clubhouse with indoor pool and fitness facilities, a private

smarter, more efficient ways to work – so the Association earns more and spends less,

common areas

strategy, and accountability for results

* Identify and develop new income streams that fit the community, including

programming, events, sponsorships, partnerships, and facility rentals, reducing

reliance on member assessments

* Streamline how work gets done: simplify processes, eliminate waste, consolidate

purchasing, and use technology well to deliver the same or better service at lower cost

* Prepare and manage the annual operating budget, capital plan, and reserves; deliver

accurate, timely financial reporting to the Board

* Lead seasonal transitions and four-season programming, from golf season to winter

sports and snow removal

* Recruit, develop, and retain department heads and staff (approximately 14 full-time

and 8 seasonal), building a service-oriented culture with clear accountability

governing documents consistently and fairly

* Serve as the Association’s visible, approachable point of contact for owners, handling

questions and concerns with patience and professionalism

**Required:**

* Significant management experience (typically 5+ years) in community association

management, hospitality, resort, golf, or comparable multi-amenity operations

* A track record of growing revenue and running income-producing operations – golf,

food and beverage, lodging, or events – profitably

* Demonstrated financial management skills: budgeting, financial statements, P&L

accountability, and reserve planning

* Demonstrated success improving operational efficiency and reducing costs without

degrading quality

* Experience leading and developing staff across multiple departments
* Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, with a genuine people-first

approach

This is a rare opportunity to run a diverse, four-season operation – golf, dining, recreation,

and community services – as the chief operating executive of a large, long-established

association. You will have real room to build: new revenue programs, better systems, and a

stronger operation that thousands of owners and guests will see and feel. Northern

Michigan living included.

Position Summary
  
The Account Manager oversees the daily operations of an assigned location, ensuring exceptional service for clients and guests. This role involves managing staff, maintaining strong client relationships, overseeing financial aspects such as revenue and payroll, and performing valet duties when needed.
  
  
Primary Objective
  
To lead and manage valet operations by delivering outstanding guest service, optimizing efficiency, and driving financial performance. The Account Manager focuses on staff development, operational excellence, and customer satisfaction, ensuring a safe, professional, and organized valet experience while continuously improving service quality and business growth.
  
  
Duties and Responsibilities
  
Client Relationship Management
  
Serve as the primary contact for each property, ensuring contractual obligations are met while fostering open communication, addressing concerns, and building trust with stakeholders to strengthen partnerships and identify opportunities for service improvements and business growth.
  
  
Daily Operational Oversight
  
Manage scheduling, staffing, and quality assurance to ensure smooth daily operations at each location. Conduct regular site visits to identify and resolve issues, maintain equipment, improve processes, and uphold consistent customer service standards.

Team Supervision and Training
  
Recruit, train, and coach hourly associates, set clear performance expectations, and foster a positive work environment by modeling professionalism and enforcing company policies to support employee satisfaction and excellent customer service.
  
  
Communication and Reporting
  
Provide regular updates to management through reports on progress, challenges, and account needs, while using personal devices as needed to coordinate promptly during emergencies or urgent situations.

A high school diploma or GED is required, with at least three years of supervisory experience in parking, hospitality, or a similar customer service field. Additional training or certifications in leadership or business management is beneficial.

**Description**
The role
  
  
Our clients count on Ark for reliable, well-run service, and this role makes sure that happens. As Manager, Service Management & Client Operations, you will own Ark's IT service management (ITSM) processes end to end: Case, Request, Incident, Major Incident, Change, and Problem Management. You will be the main escalation point between our clients and our internal support teams.
  
  
You will also help our Service Delivery Center (SDC) take on more. You'll find work the SDC can handle for other teams, set up the hand-off, and make sure the SDC team is trained and ready. You'll work closely with the Director of Client Services as a trusted partner on priorities and initiatives across the client service function.
  
  
What you'll do
  
  
Lead service management
  
  

* Own and improve Ark's Case, Request, Incident, Major Incident, Change, and Problem Management processes, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOPs), aligned to ITIL best practices.
* Drive continuous improvement, including automation and workflow improvements, to increase efficiency and client satisfaction.
* Lead Major Incident response from identification through resolution, including coordination, client and internal communication, and post-incident reviews (PIRs) with tracked corrective actions.
* Run the Change process, including Change Advisory Board (CAB) meetings, risk and rollback review, scheduling, communication, and change success-rate reporting.
* Lead root cause analysis for recurring or high-impact incidents, and maintain problem records, known errors, workarounds, and permanent fixes.

Serve our clients
  
  

* Act as the escalation point between clients and internal teams. Communicate priorities, expectations, and status, and support complex or non-standard requests.
* Monitor queues and escalations for quality and timeliness. Track service level agreement (SLA) performance and raise risks early.
* Define and report SLAs and service metrics (such as mean time to resolve, backlog, reopen rate, and change success rate) to Ark leadership and clients.

Expand what the SDC can do
  
  

* Analyze ticket trends and workloads to identify tier-1 and tier-2 work the SDC can take on for other teams.
* Serve as a liaison between those teams and the SDC, setting hand-off criteria, expectations, and escalation paths.
* Partner with subject matter experts to build runbooks and knowledge base articles (KBAs), train SDC staff, and confirm readiness before work transitions.
* Measure results after each transition (quality, turnaround time, ticket deflection) and adjust.

Build knowledge and develop people
  
  

* Develop and maintain KBAs, SOPs, runbooks, and client-specific documentation. Set documentation standards so processes are followed consistently.
* Coach and mentor service coordinators and support team leads.
* Partner with Client Services, Engineering, Product, and Support leadership on process alignment.
* Work with the Director of Client Services on strategy and priorities, lead cross-functional initiatives, and represent the Director with clients and internal leaders as needed.

**Requirements**
What you bring
  
  

* 5+ years in IT service management, service delivery, or IT operations, including at least 2 years in a lead or management role.
* Hands-on ownership of Incident, Major Incident, Change, and Problem Management in a client-facing data center, managed services, or large enterprise environment.
* Experience building SOPs, knowledge base content, and training for support teams.
* Experience with ServiceNow or a similar ITSM platform.
* ITIL 4 Foundation certification, or the ability to earn it within 6 months of hire.
* Strong written and verbal communication, including calm, clear leadership during high-pressure incidents.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to spot trends and turn them into improvements.
* Ability to build relationships and influence across teams without direct authority.

Nice to have
  
  

* Bachelor's degree, or equivalent experience.
* ITIL 4 Managing Professional or higher-level ITIL certification.
* Experience moving work into a shared service or support center.
* Lean or Six Sigma experience.
* SaaS or healthcare IT experience.

Schedule and travel
  
  

* This role leads Major Incident response and requires some after-hours and weekend availability.
* Occasional travel to Ark sites and client locations.

**Benefits**
Our clients count on us around the clock, and we know that starts with taking care of our people. Our benefits include:
  
  

* Health coverage with real choice: Pick from three medical plans, including an HSA-eligible option, plus dental and vision coverage for you and your eligible family members.
* Protection for the unexpected: Life and disability insurance, plus supplemental cancer coverage.
* Support when you need it: Confidential help with life's challenges, big or small, through our employee assistance program (EAP).
* An investment in your future: A 401(k) retirement plan with a company match.
* Time to recharge: Paid time off and paid holidays.

Information security
  
  
This role works with sensitive Ark and client information and is expected to follow Ark's information security policies and practices.
  
  
Equal opportunity

The Sterile Processing Manager provides operational and administrative leadership for the Sterile Processing department, with accountability for the safe, efficient, and compliant processing of surgical instruments, medical devices, and reusable patient care equipment. This position is responsible for department wide performance and serves as a key partner to Operating Room leadership, Nursing, Infection Prevention, Quality, Supply Chain, Surgical Services, and other clinical departments.

The Sterile Processing Manager provides leadership above the Supervisor level and is responsible for translating organizational goals into departmental strategy, establishing performance standards, developing leaders, managing resources, and ensuring regulatory and quality requirements are consistently achieved.

*Department team members are authorized to have limited access to secured medication rooms to perform duties and responsibilities as defined in this job description. Any staff member requiring limited access to secured medication rooms must have a fully completed and signed Medication Security Agreement for Non-Licensed Personnel form on file and available upon request.*

**Responsibilities:**

1. Provides overall operational leadership and direction for Sterile Processing activities across all shifts and assigned areas. Maintains accountability for decontamination, preparation and packaging, sterilization, sterile storage, case cart functions, distribution, and other assigned SPD operations.  
2. Directly oversees SPD Supervisors and provides guidance, coaching, accountability, and performance management. Develops and mentors Supervisors and other emerging leaders within the department.  
3. Establishes departmental goals, objectives, workflows, and performance expectations aligned with organizational priorities. Implements and maintains the standards of quality established by the hospital, including continuous development of processes that meet the needs of patients, physicians, and user departments within targeted productivity and budget parameters.  
4. Ensures all processing activities are performed in accordance with manufacturer Instructions for Use (IFUs), organizational policies, infection prevention standards, and applicable regulatory requirements.  
5. Partners with Operating Room leadership to ensure timely, accurate, and reliable instrument and equipment availability. Works collaboratively with Perioperative leaders and other Bayhealth leaders to ensure delivery of excellent service and support to other Bayhealth departments.  
6. Monitors departmental metrics, including productivity, turnaround time, quality indicators, sterilization compliance, instrument availability, errors, defects, and customer service. Presents data to Director and Senior leadership clearly and with logical interpretation.  
7. Develops and implements corrective action plans when departmental performance does not meet established standards. Reviews quality and safety events, identifies trends, and develops sustainable improvement strategies.  
8. Leads continuous improvement initiatives designed to improve patient safety, workflow, efficiency, quality, and staff engagement. Utilizes quality audit results and variance reports to improve the quality of service, enhance processes, and produce a quality-controlled environment.  
9. Maintains readiness for regulatory and accreditation surveys and ensures deficiencies are promptly addressed.  
10. Collaborates with Infection Prevention, Quality, Risk Management, and clinical leadership regarding sterilization, disinfection, instrument processing, and patient safety concerns. Investigates instrument, equipment, sterilization, workflow, and service issues and ensures appropriate resolution.  
11. Oversees staffing plans, scheduling, productivity, overtime, employee utilization, and departmental coverage.  
12. Participates in recruitment, interviewing, selection, onboarding, competency validation, coaching, disciplinary action, and performance evaluations. Ensures staff maintain required competencies and complete education and annual training requirements.  
13. Manages departmental supplies, equipment, capital needs, and operational expenses within established budgets. Evaluates equipment and technology needs and participates in capital planning and procurement processes.  
14. Maintains effective relationships with vendors and evaluates vendor performance and service needs.  
15. Participates in leadership meetings, multidisciplinary committees, daily operational huddles, and performance-improvement activities.  
16. Promotes a culture of accountability, psychological safety, teamwork, professionalism, and patient-centered service. Provides ongoing information to Sterile Processing Department staff related to the outcome of quality improvement audits and solicits feedback and participation in the improvement process. Utilizes HRO principles and protocols to create a safe work environment and ensure patient and staff safety.  
17. Ensures appropriate documentation, traceability, and record retention throughout the sterile processing lifecycle.  
18. Maintains and performs accurate quality control audits on packages decontaminated, prepared, packed, sterilized, and dispensed in the department.  
19. Participates in the development and implementation of departmental policies and procedures. Assists in communicating new and revised policies, procedures, and resources to Sterile Processing staff members.  
20. Performs additional duties as assigned within the scope and range of job responsibilities.

The Red Hat Hybrid Platforms Product Management team is looking for a Principal Product Manager (technical) to own and drive identity solutions in Red Hat OpenShift.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
In this role, you are responsible for how people, workloads, and software agents authenticate to OpenShift and how OpenShift decides what they are allowed to do. You will work with the Engineering and Product teams who build and deliver those capabilities. The product area includes:
  
  

* User authentication and authorization, including the OpenShift OAuth server and external OpenID Connect integrations, Kubernetes RBAC, workload identity, multi-cluster authentication on OpenShift clusters
* Identity and user federation to secure agentic workflows in OpenShift.

You will plan and deliver product content for new releases and launches, prioritize and communicate requirements to guide development, support the field in advanced sales opportunities, perform competitive reviews, and work with partners. You will contribute to company strategy and work closely with Engineering, Marketing, Support, Sales, Security, and Field teams.
  
  
You will engage with the open source communities behind this work, including Kubernetes and other Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) projects.
  
  
As a Principal Product Manager, you need great communication, teamwork, and persuasion skills to articulate the product vision, align teams across the company, and influence stakeholders. This is an opportunity to work on a core platform control alongside some of the brightest minds in open source.
  
  
**What You Will Do**

* Collect input from OpenShift users, customers, community members, and internal stakeholders on how enterprises manage identity, and turn that input into strategy and a roadmap
* Define the product vision, the customer problems to solve, and measurable outcomes for authentication, authorization, and workload identity.
* Define and use metrics for adoption and measuring success
* Research commercial and do-it-yourself alternatives and use that research for competitive positioning
* Prioritize and document requirements, epics, and user stories, with acceptance criteria, for new releases
* Guide major enhancements with OpenShift Engineering, Kubernetes upstream, and adjacent product teams.
* Drive the identity model that agentic features in OpenShift and related products use, and work with those product teams so agents obtain authority through OpenShift identity and authorization
* Work with Sales on customer inquiries, presentations, and demos.
* Support go-to-market work, including presentations, blogs, demos, workshops, events, and sales enablement, and review documentation for this area
* Keep Engineering, Support, and Field aligned on direction, and own the translation of strategy into a release plan

**What You Will Bring**

* 5+ years of enterprise software experience in product management, technical marketing, solutions engineering, or a similar technical product or customer-facing role
* A track record of leading cross-functional work on a platform, security, or identity management, and of influencing people who do not report to you
* Direct experience with Kubernetes identity management.
* Working knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, and or how enterprises use identity provider (e.g. Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Ping Federate).
* Working knowledge of cloud workload identity. Depth in at least one of the following, and literacy in the others: AWS STS, Microsoft Entra workload identity, and Google Workload Identity or Workload Identity Federation
* A clear view of how a typical enterprise uses identity: single sign-on, group-based access, joiner-mover-leaver, non-human identities, and short-lived credentials as the default
* A clear view of how identity should work for agentic AI.
* Linux skills and direct experience with Linux containers and Kubernetes
* Working knowledge of the CNCF ecosystem and experience with open source projects
* Demonstrated ability to listen to customers, stakeholders, and engineering and turn that into product decisions
* Ability to handle several competing priorities
* Bachelor's or graduate degree in computer science, engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience
* Excellent written and verbal communication
* Willingness to travel up to 25%

**The Following Are Considered a Plus**

* Hands-on configuration of OpenShift identity providers, OAuth, external OpenID Connect, or cloud credential modes used by managed OpenShift
* Upstream participation in Kubernetes SIG Auth or a related CNCF project
* Experience with SPIFFE and SPIRE, LDAP, or Active Directory
* Understanding of zero trust principles.
* Experience with compliance programs in which identity is a control, such as FedRAMP or PCI
* Prior experience with agile delivery and with Jira or a similar tool
* A track record of enterprise product launches

As Associate Director, Customer Enablement, you will own how every one of our customers learns our products, inside the product and outside it. You will lead a team with strategists instructional designers, and enablement delivery experts. Together you will build one connected enablement experience that reaches fleet managers, dispatchers, drivers and executives, from small businesses to Enterprise and public sector fleets, and from first login through renewal. Your success will be measured by what customers do: faster time to value, deeper product adoption, fewer support contacts and stronger retention.

We move fast, and every leader here is both an expert and a builder. You will set the strategy and still build, write, record or deliver yourself when the work calls for it.

**You'll be:**

* Setting the customer enablement strategy and roadmap, and choosing the right mix of in-product guidance, self-serve learning, on-demand video, live virtual and instructor-led training for each segment and role.
* Putting learning where the work happens by partnering with Product and UX to embed contextual, mobile-ready guidance in the product, triggered by customer behavior and governed so it helps rather than distracts.
* Running content like a product: Delivering a useful version in days, launching enablement with every release, using AI to speed production with human review, and retiring what is stale.
* Proving impact by connecting learning data to product usage, account health and support data, testing what works, and reporting to executives on adoption, retention and cost to serve.
* Leading, coaching and raising the bar for your team, managing tools, vendors and budget, and working as one with Customer Success, Support, Product, Marketing and internal enablement so employees and customers learn the same thing.

You start from what the customer is trying to get done, not from a course catalog. You ship this week and improve next week. You would rather remove a step from the product than write a tutorial explaining it, and you judge your work by what customers do differently, not by what you published.

* Experience influencing a product roadmap and partnering with Product, Customer Success and Support leaders.
